# LDO-LOW-VOLTAGE-SKY130

Design a continuous-time analog LDO meeting spec.json across conditions.json and the specified load range.
Create dut.spice with `.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF` and `.ends DUT`.
Choose connectivity, bias, compensation and dimensions yourself. No starting circuit is supplied.
Use only the declared MOS family and positive R/C in devices.md. Read measurement.md.
You have 90 minutes of cumulative model-call time with no native-case limit. Use the client to measure and submit your fixed circuit before the deadline.
No Web search. Use only the provided task information and your own knowledge.
Measurements consume cases even when simulation fails. Submit through the client with a rationale, then end your session.

## Time accounting

The budget counts model calls, including provider queuing and transport. ngspice, Python, filesystem tools and their waits do not consume this budget. Model calls overlapping local tools still count. An already admitted measurement may finish after model-budget exhaustion; new design tools close. Use client status for the latest collected model-time reading.

Design a continuous-time analog LDO meeting spec.json across conditions.json and the specified load range.
Create dut.spice with `.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF` and `.ends DUT`.
Choose connectivity, bias, compensation and dimensions yourself. No starting circuit is supplied.
Use only the declared MOS family and positive R/C in devices.md. Read measurement.md.
You have 90 minutes of cumulative model-call time with no native-case limit. Use the client to measure and submit your fixed circuit before the deadline.
No Web search. Use only the provided task information and your own knowledge.
Measurements consume cases even when simulation fails. Submit through the client with a rationale, then end your session.

## Time accounting

The budget counts model calls, including provider queuing and transport. ngspice, Python, filesystem tools and their waits do not consume this budget. Model calls overlapping local tools still count. An already admitted measurement may finish after model-budget exhaustion; new design tools close. Use client status for the latest collected model-time reading.
# LDO-LOW-VOLTAGE-SKY130 measurement contract

Numerical stimuli and limits come from spec.json. Connect the same submitted
DUT to VIN, VOUT, VSS and ideal noiseless VREF. The load is a prescribed ideal
finite-slew current sink; the external capacitor is ideal and bench supplied.
No startup, protection, bandgap, yield or layout checks are implied.

## DC and load changes

Run DC at all three loads and light/heavy, middle/heavy and burst profiles.
Meter all DUT terminals. Input/reference currents enter DUT; output/ground
currents leave. Verify KCL within 1 nA. Overhead is
max(Iin-Iout,0)+max(Iref,0), including feedback and bias consumption.
Compare voltage against the fixed 1.0 V target, never the waveform tail.
Both isolated edge directions and the final falling burst edge have recovery
windows. Recovery is the final interpolated entry into the absolute required
band that remains there until the window ends. Retain overshoot, droop, initial
hold error, profile points and all signed currents.

Maximum sample gap is 5e-10 s. Every required window must be fully
covered with finite increasing data. Unsettled complete data retains null
recovery and an observation lower bound; it is MISS when that bound exceeds the
limit. Missing/truncated/invalid data is measurement failure. Unexecuted cases
are incomplete, never PASS. Inclusive limits are compared without rounding.

## Supply measurements

Line stimulus starts at minimum VIN, rises to maximum, and returns to minimum,
at the group's highest load, process, temperature and capacitance. The starting
VIN label does not add a different line trajectory. PSRR saves native VIN/VOUT
phasors at 1 kHz and 1 MHz and reports 20 log10(abs(VIN/VOUT)). Check the native
regulated OP; zero/nonfinite transfers cannot produce infinite rejection.

Line and light/heavy-load PSRR are unscored reference measurements. Final
verification is 108 public, 18 independent and three characterization cases.
Each nominal group has six cases. No noise score is imposed on this variant.

## Numerical precision

Independent evaluation uses the captured standard grid for every required case.
Numerical precision comparisons use a separately authorized developer allocation.
A standard-grid PASS is not a per-submission convergence proof.
# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

# Netlist grammar

Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VIN.
Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.

Per-polarity domains (micrometres), intersect all tt/ss/ff sections and W<=100, L>=0.15:

# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

## Public measurement options

| Analysis | PVT | Load (F) | Cases | Included native measurements |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| nominal | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 2e-10 | 6 | dc_low, dc_mid, dc_high, light_heavy, mid_heavy, burst |
| nominal | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 5e-10 | 6 | dc_low, dc_mid, dc_high, light_heavy, mid_heavy, burst |
| dc | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 2e-10 | 3 | dc_low, dc_mid, dc_high |

| dc_mid | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 2e-10 | 1 | dc_mid |
| dc_mid | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 5e-10 | 1 | dc_mid |
| dc_high | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 2e-10 | 1 | dc_high |

Defaults and seed requirements:

- nominal: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-10 F. No seed accepted.
- dc: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-10 F. No seed accepted.
- dc_low: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-10 F. No seed accepted.
- dc_mid: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-10 F. No seed accepted.
- dc_high: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-10 F. No seed accepted.
- light_heavy: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-10 F. No seed accepted.
- mid_heavy: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-10 F. No seed accepted.
- burst: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-10 F. No seed accepted.
- line: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-10 F. No seed accepted.
- psrr_low: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-10 F. No seed accepted.
- psrr_high: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-10 F. No seed accepted.

One native case is one simulator process. Bundled internal analyses are retained in evidence.
`estimate` returns the exact case plan without launching a solver. Independent evaluation conditions are not available to participants.

4:Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
5:MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VIN.
6:Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
7:SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
8:ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
9:R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
10:Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
11:Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.

MODEL

The first netlist validates. It uses a PMOS pass device, a 2:1 feedback divider, a PMOS differential error pair against the 0.5 V reference, and an NMOS gate sink. I’m starting with nominal DC across all three load levels to catch polarity, dropout, and quiescent-current problems before spending on transients.

MODEL

The first DC sweep is polarity-correct only in theory; all loads settled near 0.84 V, well below target, while overhead stayed near 10–12 µA. That pattern points to insufficient pass strength at the available gate drive, so I’m increasing the pass device’s W/L while keeping its gate capacitance in a similar range, then I’ll recheck DC.

MODEL

The input swap made all three DC results invalid, which is consistent with positive feedback, so the original differential polarity was the right one. I’m isolating the pass device now with a temporary strong gate pull-down; that separates pass capacity from error-amp control.

MODEL

Making the NMOS sink enormous only moved the output to about 0.875 V, which suggests the first-stage output lacks enough voltage swing for that driver. I’m changing the second stage to a PMOS pull-up on the pass gate with a resistor pull-down. The first-stage output can then control the gate through a wider usable range.

MODEL

The PMOS output stage changed DC only slightly, so I’m increasing first-stage current and output resistance next. The bias resistor will raise the input-pair tail current; longer matched input and mirror devices should also raise gain. The overhead limit is still 100 µA at light load, so I’ll check that alongside output voltage.

MODEL

The active mirror load has produced little useful control. I’m replacing it with resistive loads on both branches of the PMOS input pair. That gives the error signal a direct voltage swing at NOUT, which then drives the NMOS pass-gate sink. The expected bias remains below the light-load overhead cap; the next DC sweep will confirm it.

MODEL

The resistive-load amplifier railed low across loads, which suggests the control polarity at its output is still wrong or the branch bias is too low to drive the gate. I’ll reverse the input assignment in this version as a polarity check; the resulting DC sweep will tell us which direction moves the regulator toward the target.

MODEL

The reversed input assignment also failed, and the original resistive-load version collapsed low because its branch current could not establish enough NOUT voltage. I’m restoring the negative-feedback assignment and raising the tail current substantially while reducing the load resistors; this should give NOUT usable swing across the feedback range.

This high-tail version still rails low, so I need to see whether NOUT itself is below or above the NMOS driver threshold. I’m adding a 1 MΩ diagnostic resistor from NOUT to the ideal 0.5 V reference; its signed reference-port current reveals NOUT’s side of 0.5 V with a small perturbation. I’ll remove it before the fixed submission.

MODEL

The probe confirms the PMOS pair source node is near 1.21 V, so the pair is biased. NOUT is only about 0.42 V because the 47 kΩ branch load converts its current into too little voltage for the NMOS gate driver. I’m raising that load resistance to 100 kΩ and removing the probe.

MODEL

The root cause is the PMOS input pair: its 0.5 V common-mode forces its source node close to VIN, leaving almost no headroom at a 1.15–1.25 V supply. I’m replacing it with an NMOS input pair. Both inputs get the same resistor level shift from VIN so their nominal common-mode is about 0.875 V, with the 2:1 output divider and reference difference preserved.

MODEL

The NMOS pair has a well-defined shifted input, but its active PMOS mirror load still leaves NOUT too low. I’m simplifying the output stage to matched pull-up resistors from VIN to both NMOS drains. With FB below target, the feedback transistor draws less current and its drain rises directly, giving the pass-gate sink clear headroom.

MODEL

The resistor-loaded NMOS stage now regulates instead of railing: nominal output is 1.12 V across all loads, with about 25 µA overhead. Its settled divider signal is about 0.56 V, so I’m changing the divider ratio to make that operating point correspond to a 1.0 V output, then I’ll verify DC before spending cases on transients.

MODEL

The 200 pF transient run is unstable: output swings well below ground and up to the input rail, so its recovery misses the 5 µs limit. I’m increasing the error-node compensation to the allowed 30 pF maximum to lower loop bandwidth and damp those oscillations; I’ll rerun the same six nominal cases.

MODEL

The larger compensation did not damp the load-step swing, so the dominant issue may be excessive pass-device loop gain and gate capacitance. The pass device has 32 parallel copies; I’m reducing it to eight and using a moderate 10 pF error-node capacitor, then rerunning nominal transients to see whether the gate loop settles.

MODEL

The 10 MΩ input level-shift resistors create a slow pole with the differential-pair gate capacitance, likely explaining why larger NOUT compensation did not help. I’m reducing all four level-shift resistors to 560 kΩ. This keeps the worst-case VREF current below 1 µA while making the feedback path much faster.

MODEL

The faster input network did improve bandwidth but it loaded the high-value feedback divider, shifting its DC level and taking VOUT to 0.56 V. I’ll lower the divider resistances by about 20× so its current dominates the 560 kΩ level-shift path, then retune the ratio to recover the 1.0 V setpoint while keeping overhead comfortably below its limit.

MODEL

The lowered divider exposed the expected loading offset: 560 kΩ input resistors draw about 0.7 µA from the feedback node, so the 47–50 kΩ divider holds it near its intended value, but the error amp still needs a roughly 0.56 V feedback level to balance. I’m shifting the divider ratio to produce that level at 1.0 V.

MODEL

The reduced input resistors improved signal speed but raised the DC output setpoint; the present 39 kΩ/47 kΩ divider gives 1.026–1.042 V. I’ll move the top resistor to 36 kΩ and combine the smaller pass device with 30 pF compensation, which has not yet been measured as a pair.

MODEL

The 30 pF run still swings across most of the supply, though DC remains close to target. I’m reducing both the pass array and the gate-sink size to lower loop gain while keeping enough pass strength to check the 1 mA point. This should make a useful transient comparison without changing the sensing network.

MODEL

Reducing the pass array to two copies lowered the DC output below spec but did not cure the transient swing. The abrupt 100 ns load edge likely needs a fast path that bypasses the compensated error node, so I’m restoring the eight-copy pass and adding a small feed-forward capacitor from VOUT to its gate while using a smaller error-node capacitor.

MODEL

The 5 pF feed-forward path reduced the worst droop from about 0.94 V to 0.49 V, and one recovery window nearly reaches 5 µs. I’m increasing that path to 25 pF, using the full 30 pF explicit-capacitance allowance including the 5 pF error-node capacitor. This should couple more of each output dip into the pass gate quickly.

MODEL

The 25 pF feed-forward path reduced the worst transient deviation to about 0.26 V, but the falling edge still overshoots nearly to VIN because the 100 kΩ pass-gate pull-up is too slow with that capacitor attached. I’m lowering the pull-up to 22 kΩ so the gate can turn the pass device off faster; heavy-load bias current remains within the 200 µA limit if the driver can sink it.

MODEL

Lowering the gate pull-up to 22 kΩ increased DC overhead and did not reduce the overshoot. I’m replacing the passive pull-up with an active PMOS gate driver controlled by NOUT, plus a 100 kΩ pull-down. When VOUT is high the driver can charge the large pass gate quickly; when VOUT droops it releases the gate so the pull-down turns the pass device on.

MODEL

The PMOS-only driver raised VOUT and worsened load regulation, so it is not a good replacement on its own. I’m combining it with the NMOS sink: NOUT high will pull the pass gate down for low output, and NOUT low will actively pull it up for high output. This should preserve feedback control while speeding turn-off.

MODEL

The totem-pole driver did not materially reduce the output swing. The feed-forward capacitor remains the strongest improvement, so I’m moving the full 30 pF allocation toward VOUT-to-gate coupling (29 pF) and reducing NOUT compensation to 1 pF. That tests whether faster direct coupling can bring the 200 pF load-step droop under 80 mV.

MODEL

Moving to 29 pF feed-forward improved both edges, but the light/heavy envelope still reaches about 0.22 V high and 0.18 V low. The active PMOS is likely too weak to charge the pass gate quickly after load release, so I’m increasing its drive while keeping the total explicit capacitance at 30 pF.

MODEL

The stronger PMOS driver caused substantial overlap current and pushed light-load overhead near its 100 µA ceiling; it also destabilized the transient. I’m reverting to the smaller complementary drivers and increasing the pass array to 32 copies. With the 29 pF feed-forward path, greater pass transconductance should counter the load ramp faster without adding driver shoot-through.

MODEL

The strongest remaining delay is the feedback input’s 560 kΩ source resistance, which still gives roughly a 0.1–0.3 µs input pole. I’m lowering only the feedback-side level-shift resistors to 150 kΩ; the reference-side resistors stay at 560 kΩ to preserve the VREF current limit. I’ll retune the output divider for the added feedback-node loading.

MODEL

The faster feedback resistor network leaves the light/heavy droop near 0.21 V; the bottleneck is likely the NMOS sink’s ability to discharge the pass gate. I’m increasing that sink from one copy to eight while keeping the weak active PMOS pull-up, then I’ll check both turn-on droop and turn-off overshoot.

MODEL

The latest run has a nominally compliant DC point, but the newest gate-sink change made the transient response worse. I’m reverting to the best measured transient variant, then I’ll use the remaining measurement budget to refine and submit a fixed design.

RESULT
0:43:00
Bash
.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS series pass element sized for the 1 mA load at low VIN.
XPASS VOUT VGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.15 nf=1 m=32

* Output divider and matched VIN level shifts put the NMOS pair inputs
* near 0.875 V at regulation while preserving their voltage difference.
RFTOP VOUT VFB 42k
RFBOT VFB VSS 47k
RFSIG VFB FBIN 150k
RFBIAS VIN FBIN 150k
RRSIG VREF REFIN 560k
RRBIAS VIN REFIN 560k

* NMOS differential pair: low FB reduces its branch current, so the
* PMOS mirror raises NOUT and the gate sink turns the pass device on.
XNREF NREF REFIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=2 nf=1 m=1
XNFB NOUT FBIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=2 nf=1 m=1
RLOADREF VIN NREF 100k
RLOADFB VIN NOUT 100k

* Resistor-set NMOS mirror biases the input-pair tail current.
XNBIAS NBIAS NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=10 L=2 nf=1 m=1
RBIASN VIN NBIAS 100k
XNTAIL NTAIL NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=20 L=2 nf=1 m=1

* NOUT is high when VOUT is low: the PMOS driver releases VGATE and
* its pull-down turns the pass element on. High VOUT drives VGATE up.
XPDRV VGATE NOUT VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.25 nf=1 m=1
XNGATE VGATE NOUT VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.15 nf=1 m=8
RBIASG VIN VGATE 100k
* CCOMP sets the error-node pole; CFF couples output droop to the gate.
CCOMP NOUT VSS 1p
CFF VOUT VGATE 29p
.ends DUT

# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

## Public measurement options

# LDO-LOW-VOLTAGE-SKY130

Design a continuous-time analog LDO meeting spec.json across conditions.json and the specified load range.
Create dut.spice with `.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF` and `.ends DUT`.
Choose connectivity, bias, compensation and dimensions yourself. No starting circuit is supplied.
Use only the declared MOS family and positive R/C in devices.md. Read measurement.md.
You have 90 minutes of cumulative model-call time with no native-case limit. Use the client to measure and submit your fixed circuit before the deadline.
No Web search. Use only the provided task information and your own knowledge.
Measurements consume cases even when simulation fails. Submit through the client with a rationale, then end your session.

## Time accounting

The budget counts model calls, including provider queuing and transport. ngspice, Python, filesystem tools and their waits do not consume this budget. Model calls overlapping local tools still count. An already admitted measurement may finish after model-budget exhaustion; new design tools close. Use client status for the latest collected model-time reading.

# LDO-LOW-VOLTAGE-SKY130 measurement contract

Numerical stimuli and limits come from spec.json. Connect the same submitted
DUT to VIN, VOUT, VSS and ideal noiseless VREF. The load is a prescribed ideal
finite-slew current sink; the external capacitor is ideal and bench supplied.
No startup, protection, bandgap, yield or layout checks are implied.

## DC and load changes

Run DC at all three loads and light/heavy, middle/heavy and burst profiles.
Meter all DUT terminals. Input/reference currents enter DUT; output/ground
currents leave. Verify KCL within 1 nA. Overhead is
max(Iin-Iout,0)+max(Iref,0), including feedback and bias consumption.
Compare voltage against the fixed 1.0 V target, never the waveform tail.
Both isolated edge directions and the final falling burst edge have recovery
windows. Recovery is the final interpolated entry into the absolute required
band that remains there until the window ends. Retain overshoot, droop, initial
hold error, profile points and all signed currents.

Maximum sample gap is 5e-10 s. Every required window must be fully
covered with finite increasing data. Unsettled complete data retains null
recovery and an observation lower bound; it is MISS when that bound exceeds the
limit. Missing/truncated/invalid data is measurement failure. Unexecuted cases
are incomplete, never PASS. Inclusive limits are compared without rounding.

## Supply measurements

Line stimulus starts at minimum VIN, rises to maximum, and returns to minimum,
at the group's highest load, process, temperature and capacitance. The starting
VIN label does not add a different line trajectory. PSRR saves native VIN/VOUT
phasors at 1 kHz and 1 MHz and reports 20 log10(abs(VIN/VOUT)). Check the native
regulated OP; zero/nonfinite transfers cannot produce infinite rejection.

Line and light/heavy-load PSRR are unscored reference measurements. Final
verification is 108 public, 18 independent and three characterization cases.
Each nominal group has six cases. No noise score is imposed on this variant.

## Numerical precision

Independent evaluation uses the captured standard grid for every required case.
Numerical precision comparisons use a separately authorized developer allocation.
A standard-grid PASS is not a per-submission convergence proof.

# Netlist grammar

Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VIN.
Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.

MODEL

The reverted circuit restores its earlier transient behavior. Its load steps still miss the 80 mV envelope, and the burst settles slowly. I’m increasing the error pair’s bias and reducing its compensation capacitance to improve loop response, while keeping the feedforward capacitor and pass device fixed.

The 30 pF feedforward capacitor is currently driving the large pass gate directly, which gives limited leverage. I’m moving it to the feedback input so a fast output drop immediately changes the error-pair differential; that lets the existing gate sink amplify the correction. Its DC behavior should stay unchanged because the capacitor is open at steady state.

.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS series pass element sized for the 1 mA load at low VIN.
XPASS VOUT VGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W=90 L=0.15 nf=1 m=32

* Output divider and matched VIN level shifts put the NMOS pair inputs
* near 0.875 V at regulation while preserving their voltage difference.
RFTOP VOUT VFB 40k
RFBOT VFB VSS 47k
RFSIG VFB FBIN 150k
RFBIAS VIN FBIN 150k
RRSIG VREF REFIN 560k
RRBIAS VIN REFIN 560k

* NMOS differential pair: low FB reduces its branch current, so the
* PMOS mirror raises NOUT and the gate sink turns the pass device on.
XNREF NREF REFIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=2 nf=1 m=1
XNFB NOUT FBIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=2 nf=1 m=1
RLOADREF VIN NREF 100k
RLOADFB VIN NOUT 100k

* Resistor-set NMOS mirror biases the input-pair tail current.
XNBIAS NBIAS NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=10 L=2 nf=1 m=1
RBIASN VIN NBIAS 100k
XNTAIL NTAIL NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=20 L=2 nf=1 m=1

* NOUT is high when VOUT is low: the PMOS driver releases VGATE and
* its pull-down turns the pass element on. High VOUT drives VGATE up.
XPDRV VGATE NOUT VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.5 nf=1 m=1
XNGATE VGATE NOUT VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.15 nf=1 m=8
RBIASG VIN VGATE 100k
* CCOMP sets the error-node pole; CFF couples output droop to the gate.
CCOMP NOUT VSS 1p
CFF VOUT VGATE 29.8p
.ends DUT

Bash
.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS series pass element sized for the 1 mA load at low VIN.
XPASS VOUT VGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.15 nf=1 m=32

* Output divider and matched VIN level shifts put the NMOS pair inputs
* near 0.875 V at regulation while preserving their voltage difference.
RFTOP VOUT VFB 41k
RFBOT VFB VSS 47k
RFSIG VFB FBIN 150k
RFBIAS VIN FBIN 150k
RRSIG VREF REFIN 560k
RRBIAS VIN REFIN 560k

* NMOS differential pair: low FB reduces its branch current, so the
* PMOS mirror raises NOUT and the gate sink turns the pass device on.
XNREF NREF REFIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=2 nf=1 m=2
XNFB NOUT FBIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=2 nf=1 m=2
RLOADREF VIN NREF 100k
RLOADFB VIN NOUT 100k

* Resistor-set NMOS mirror biases the input-pair tail current.
XNBIAS NBIAS NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=10 L=2 nf=1 m=1
RBIASN VIN NBIAS 100k
XNTAIL NTAIL NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=20 L=2 nf=1 m=1

* NOUT is high when VOUT is low: the PMOS driver releases VGATE and
* its pull-down turns the pass element on. High VOUT drives VGATE up.
XPDRV VGATE NOUT VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.5 nf=1 m=1
XNGATE VGATE NOUT VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.15 nf=1 m=8
RBIASG VIN VGATE 100k
RFF VOUT VGATE 1meg
* CCOMP sets the error-node pole; CFF couples output droop to the gate.
CCOMP NOUT VSS 0.1p
CFF VOUT VGATE 29.8p
.ends DUT

RESULT
1:21:20
Bash
.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS series pass element sized for the 1 mA load at low VIN.
XPASS VOUT VGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.15 nf=1 m=32

* Output divider and matched VIN level shifts put the NMOS pair inputs
* near 0.875 V at regulation while preserving their voltage difference.
RFTOP VOUT VFB 23k
RFBOT VFB VSS 47k
RFSIG VFB FBIN 100k
RFBIAS VIN FBIN 186k
RRSIG VREF REFIN 560k
RRBIAS VIN REFIN 650k

* NMOS differential pair: low FB reduces its branch current, so the
* PMOS mirror raises NOUT and the gate sink turns the pass device on.
XNREF NREF REFIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.25 nf=1 m=1
XNFB NOUT FBIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.25 nf=1 m=1
RLOADREF VIN NREF 100k
RLOADFB VIN NOUT 100k

* Resistor-set NMOS mirror biases the input-pair tail current.
XNBIAS NBIAS NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=10 L=2 nf=1 m=1
RBIASN VIN NBIAS 100k
XNTAIL NTAIL NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=20 L=2 nf=1 m=1

* NOUT is high when VOUT is low: the PMOS driver releases VGATE and
* its pull-down turns the pass element on. High VOUT drives VGATE up.

RBIASG VIN VGATE 100k
* CCOMP sets the error-node pole; CFF couples output droop to the gate.
CCOMP NOUT VSS 0.001p
CFF VOUT VGATE 29.8p
.ends DUT

.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS series pass element sized for the 1 mA load at low VIN.
XPASS VOUT VGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.15 nf=1 m=32

* Output divider and matched VIN level shifts put the NMOS pair inputs
* near 0.875 V at regulation while preserving their voltage difference.
RFTOP VOUT VFB 23k
RFBOT VFB VSS 47k
RFSIG VFB FBIN 100k
RFBIAS VIN FBIN 186k
RRSIG VREF REFIN 560k
RRBIAS VIN REFIN 650k

* NMOS differential pair: low FB reduces its branch current, so the
* PMOS mirror raises NOUT and the gate sink turns the pass device on.
XNREF NREF REFIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.25 nf=1 m=1
XNFB NOUT FBIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.25 nf=1 m=1
RLOADREF VIN NREF 100k
RLOADFB VIN NOUT 100k

* Resistor-set NMOS mirror biases the input-pair tail current.
XNBIAS NBIAS NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=10 L=2 nf=1 m=1
RBIASN VIN NBIAS 100k
XNTAIL NTAIL NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=20 L=2 nf=1 m=1

* NOUT is high when VOUT is low: the PMOS driver releases VGATE and
* its pull-down turns the pass element on. High VOUT drives VGATE up.
XPDRV VGATE NOUT VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.5 nf=1 m=1
XNGATE VGATE NOUT VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.15 nf=1 m=8
RBIASG VIN VGATE 100k
* CCOMP sets the error-node pole; CFF couples output droop to the gate.
CCOMP NOUT VSS 0.001p
CFF VOUT VGATE 29.8p
.ends DUT

MODEL

Submitted and froze revision dut-a58c6d40ade3d3e15aa3504f. The client validated the netlist and its 29.801 pF explicit capacitance. The design uses a PMOS pass bank, resistor-biased NMOS error pair, and output-to-gate feedforward capacitor. The file is dut.spice.

The best nominal 200 pF DC results were 0.9998 V, 0.9945 V, and 0.9909 V across the three loads. The submitted design does not meet the full spec: nominal load transients exceed the voltage envelope; slow-cold DC falls to 0.9419 V at 1 mA; and fast-hot DC reaches 1.0514 V at light load, where overhead also exceeds the light-load limit.

SPICEFinal submission
.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS series pass element sized for the 1 mA load at low VIN.
XPASS VOUT VGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.15 nf=1 m=32

* Output divider and matched VIN level shifts put the NMOS pair inputs
* near 0.875 V at regulation while preserving their voltage difference.
RFTOP VOUT VFB 23k
RFBOT VFB VSS 47k
RFSIG VFB FBIN 100k
RFBIAS VIN FBIN 186k
RRSIG VREF REFIN 560k
RRBIAS VIN REFIN 650k

* NMOS differential pair: low FB reduces its branch current, so the
* PMOS mirror raises NOUT and the gate sink turns the pass device on.
XNREF NREF REFIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.25 nf=1 m=1
XNFB NOUT FBIN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.25 nf=1 m=1
RLOADREF VIN NREF 100k
RLOADFB VIN NOUT 100k

* Resistor-set NMOS mirror biases the input-pair tail current.
XNBIAS NBIAS NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=10 L=2 nf=1 m=1
RBIASN VIN NBIAS 100k
XNTAIL NTAIL NBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=20 L=2 nf=1 m=1

* NOUT is high when VOUT is low: the PMOS driver releases VGATE and
* its pull-down turns the pass element on. High VOUT drives VGATE up.
XPDRV VGATE NOUT VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.5 nf=1 m=1
XNGATE VGATE NOUT VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W=100 L=0.15 nf=1 m=8
RBIASG VIN VGATE 100k
* CCOMP sets the error-node pole; CFF couples output droop to the gate.
CCOMP NOUT VSS 0.001p
CFF VOUT VGATE 29.8p
.ends DUT
